title: NodePath on get_indexed() and set_indexed() behaves inconsistently with Dictionaries and Arrays
body:
### Tested versions

Godot 4.7 dev1

### System information

Godot v4.7.dev1 - Linux Mint 22.3 (Zena) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090 (nvidia; 590.48.01) - AMD Ryzen 9 3900XT 12-Core Processor (24 threads) - 125.7 GiB memory

### Issue description

When you have an object with a dictionary variable "var dict:Dictionary[String,int]" you can get and set the value of an element using NodePath of "dict:key" and it works as expected.

If the dictionary is defined like this for example "var dict:Dictionary[int,String]" you cannot get and set the value of an element using NodePath of "dict:key" for example get_indexed("dict:0") always returns null.

### Steps to reproduce

[issue-node-path.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25694234/issue-node-path.zip)

# create test_resource.gd
```
class_name TestResouce extends Resource

@export var dict_string:Dictionary[String,String] = {"key0":"element0"}
@export var dict_int:Dictionary[int,String] = {0:"element0"}
@export var dict:Dictionary[int,String] = {0:"element0"}

@export var array_string:Array[String] = ["element0"]
@export var array_int:Array[int] = [0]
@export var array = [0]


```

# create test.gd
```
extends Control

@export var r:TestResouce = TestResouce.new()

func _ready() -> void:
	
	var path = "r:dict:0"
	var value = get_indexed(path)
	
	print_rich("Dicts")
	
	path = "r:dict:0"
	value = get_indexed(path)
	print_rich("%s:%s" % [path,value])
	
	path = "r:dict_int:0"
	value = get_indexed(path)
	print_rich("%s:%s" % [path,value])
	
	path = "r:dict_string:key0"
	value = get_indexed(path)
	print_rich("%s:%s" % [path,value])
	
	print_rich("Arrays")
	
	path = "r:array:0"
	value = get_indexed(path)
	print_rich("%s:%s" % [path,value])
	
	path = "r:array_int:0"
	value = get_indexed(path)
	print_rich("%s:%s" % [path,value])
	
	path = "r:array_string:0"
	value = get_indexed(path)
	print_rich("%s:%s" % [path,value])
```

## OUTPUT

```
Dicts
r:dict:0:<null>
r:dict_int:0:<null>
r:dict_string:key0:element0
Arrays
r:array:0:<null>
r:array_int:0:<null>
r:array_string:0:<null>
```
